text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Blocks(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jump(x) ::: x jumps when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Man(x) ::: x is a man.
Michael ::: the individual Michael.
Windy ::: the individual Windy.
Shooting(x, y) ::: x is shooting at y.

Premises:
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) → Blocks(x, y)) ::: If x is taller than y, then x can block y's shooting.
Taller(Michael, y) for all y ≠ Michael ::: Michael is taller than everyone else.
∀x ∀y ∀z (Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z) → Taller(x, z)) ::: Transitivity of taller relation.
Taller(Peter, Michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
¬Blocks(Windy, Michael) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
∀x (Jump(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Anyone who jumps when shooting is a great shooter.
Michael ::: is a man.
Windy ::: is a man.

Conclusion:
GreatShooter(Windy) ::: Windy is a great shooter.
